title: Delhi High Court: Section 9 Interim Relief Unavailable in Electricity Dispute Where SERC Can Act
case_name: Enerica Infra 3 Pvt. Ltd. v. NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam Ltd. & Anr.
card_summary: Justice Tushar Rao Gedela dismissed a Section 9 petition by Enerica Infra 3 to stop NTPC Vidyut Vyapar Nigam and UP Power Transmission Corporation from encashing bank guarantees worth Rs. 52.20 crore, after Enerica terminated a battery storage project deal. Section 94(2) of the Electricity Act gives the SERC interim powers like a court's, so the dispute belonged before the Commission, not under Section 9.
card_tip: Where a power-sector counterparty is SERC-regulated, seek interim relief from the Commission first; a Section 9 petition risks dismissal once the Commission can grant equivalent relief.
verification_notes: Confirmed from LiveLawBiz's report, which gives the case number, bench and reasoning, cross-checked against the judgment copy it hosts; both agree on the amount of the bank guarantees, the August 2026 termination date and the holding on SERC jurisdiction.
